reasoning: Minnie claims an alcove visit at 6:44 on the service clock. Security records make that impossible: curtain locked from 6:38 to 7:00. Brass clock error cannot rescue an explicitly service-clock claim.

She also claims adjusting an internal lamp. The actual installation photograph shows an open steel cradle with an external spotlight and side label rail. The enclosed cabinet and internal lamp exist only in the superseded proposal.

Several other late visitors lie about their timing but describe actual installed features. Several early visitors, including my innocent role, describe nonexistent cabinet features but do not use the impossible late visit as their toast-period alibi. Minnie combines both defects.

Her acknowledged prior salon business supplies a possible opportunity to contaminate the empty coupe. Threatened payment, donor demands and lighting conflict give a plausible motive. Shared toxin/key/linen access alone identifies nobody.
experience: I had to compare records against two different types of dishonest accounts rather than just notice one liar. The photographs were useful: I could see the cabinet-versus-cradle distinction immediately. As a reserved evidence-focused guest I would participate comfortably through named questions, but remembering sixteen spoken accounts without being able to revisit them would be substantially harder than reading this persistent transcript.
confusion: My innocent Frank account describes an obsolete installation. A short private rule explaining that my printed cover story may conceal an unrelated secret, and that I must stick to it until Coming Clean, would prevent me from improvising a correction.
The distinction between gallery, balcony, alcove and salon is essential. A large labeled plan available throughout the evening would help.

It is difficult to prove personal poisoning from the offered evidence. Minnie is the best supported suspect because of a compounded false account, not because a physical trace specifically identifies her.
repetitive_text: Multiple late visitors use exactly 'My other business that evening is not something I wanted Grant announcing over dinner.'
Multiple early visitors use the same 'Near the toast I was outside the enclosure ... dealing with my other business' structure.
Closing Act II by repeating the same opening line used in Act I sounds like a script stamp rather than a character voice.
accidental_giveaway: Minnie alone says she had dealt with business around Grant's salon in this Act II transcript. Other suspects should have equally plausible salon contact; otherwise that sentence narrows the field before the installation comparison.
improvements: Give each suspect a specific, distinct secret-covering sentence, especially the opportunity statements.
Include plausible salon contact for several innocents so Minnie is not uniquely linked to the poisoned vessel.
Keep the installation proposal and actual photograph large and available for visual comparison, and make the dates easy to read.
Permit targeted rereads of printed testimony when asked by name; do not require everyone to remember every timing sentence after one hearing.
Test with actual humans before claiming the difficulty is calibrated. Persistent transcripts make this simulation much easier to solve.
limitations: Independent scripted sixteen-character assessment; no live interaction, interruptions, missing clues or real party conditions. Stage files were read in order, and both earlier feedback files were saved before later stages.
